equation_request.abstract: The elementary gates are basic building blocks of quantum logic circuit. They should be simple, efficient, and easy to implement. In this article, we propose the ternary controlled X (TCX) gate or the ternary controlled Z (TCZ) gate as the two-qutrit elementary gate, which is universal when assisted by arbitrary one-qutrit gates. Based on Cartan decomposition, we give the one-qutrit elementary gates. Also, we discuss the physical implementation of these elementary gates and show that they are feasible with current technology. Then we investigate the synthesis of some important ternary gates, such as the ternary SWAP gate, ternary Toffoli gates and Muthukrishnan-Stroud gates. Finally we extend these elementary gates to a more general case for qudit systems. This work provides a unified description for the synthesis of both binary and multi-valued quantum circuits.

specification.problem: Specify the two-qutrit ternary controlled-X (TCX) and controlled-Z (TCZ) gates as elementary entangling gates, and relate them to one another, as a minimal basis for ternary quantum circuit synthesis.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Only the standard definitions of the qutrit X and Z gates, a controlled-X gate (TCX) and a controlled-Z gate (TCZ) with a tiny two-qutrit instance, and the Fourier-conjugation relation between TCX and TCZ. Outside scope: the Cartan decomposition of one-qutrit gates, the universality proof, physical implementations, SWAP/Toffoli/Muthukrishnan-Stroud synthesis, and the general qudit extension.

symbols.meaning: ternary controlled-X gate; control first, target second (assumed convention)

equations.label: Qutrit X and Z
equations.description: Generalized Pauli shift and clock gates for qutrits.
equations.justification: Standard qutrit Weyl-Heisenberg operators; the abstract does not give explicit definitions.
assumptions: The paper's X and Z may differ in convention.

equations.label: TCX definition
equations.description: Controlled shift: target is shifted by the control value, i.e. X^c is applied to the target.
equations.justification: A common qutrit generalization of CNOT; the paper's exact TCX definition (e.g. control on a single level) is not stated in the abstract.
assumptions: Control value c applies X^c to the target

equations.label: TCZ definition
equations.description: Controlled phase gate applying Z^c on the target.
equations.justification: Natural counterpart of TCX; the paper's exact definition is not given in the abstract.
assumptions: Z^c is applied to the target

equations.label: TCX-TCZ relation
equations.description: TCX is equal to TCZ conjugated by Fourier gates on the target, up to the sign or ordering convention of F, which fixes whether TCZ' is TCZ or its inverse.
equations.justification: Standard fact that F maps X to Z (or Z^-1) by conjugation. The abstract only says TCX or TCZ can serve as the elementary gate, which suggests this equivalence but does not state it.
assumptions: F convention chosen so F X F^dagger is Z or Z^-1
TCZ' denotes TCZ or its inverse depending on convention

specification.initial_state: Illustrative instance (assumed): |c,t> = |1>|2>, giving TCX -> |1>|0> and TCZ -> omega^2 |1>|2>.

steps.description: Prepare the two-qutrit basis state |c>|t>, with the control register ordered first.
Apply TCX as the assumed controlled shift.
Alternatively apply TCZ, or realize TCX from TCZ via Fourier conjugation on the target.

assumptions: Gate definitions follow common qutrit conventions, not necessarily the paper's.
No Cartan decomposition or universality equations are reconstructed.
missing_information: Paper's exact definitions of TCX and TCZ
Cartan decomposition of the one-qutrit elementary gates
Universality proof and synthesis constructions for SWAP, Toffoli and Muthukrishnan-Stroud gates
